stagesHelp: Ages, periods and revolutions on the ruler
laneNamesHelp: Field and subfield labels on the left
encIntro: Pick an advance from the index or the tree.
aSpanValue: From the first knapped stones, 3.3 million years ago, to today
aText: A map of how humankind learned to make things. Each card is a discovery, a technique, a material or an invention, placed at its date and joined to what it needed and to what it later made possible. Nobody knows how to make a whole pencil: here you can see why.
aMoveText: Drag to move and use the wheel to zoom. A right-button double click returns to the full view.
aTimeText: The ruler at the bottom shows dates and the stages of history. It stretches where there are more advances so none is hidden.
aCardsText: Click a card to see what it is, what it needed and what it made possible. Striped cards are ideas that were abandoned or proved false.
aInstallHint: To install it, use your browser’s “Install” or “Add to Home Screen” option.
aV010: First edition: the navigable tree with its time ruler, a card for each advance with what it requires and what it makes possible, search, filters and a first encyclopedia.
aV020: The tree nearly triples in size: 2,351 advances in 22 fields, with every chemical element, detailed computing, medieval mathematics, weapons, railways, spaceflight, astronomy, geology, music and economics. The time ruler now stretches down to months, weeks and days.
aTimeText2: The wheel over the ruler stretches time only, down to months, weeks and days.
aNote: A project by Alejandro Pico. The tree grows in stages; early dates are approximate and marked as such.
progressiveHelp: Card texts are downloaded when opened; when off, everything is downloaded at start
aV030: The tree grows to 3,779 advances: materials since prehistory, optics and acoustics, electrical components, nuclear power and fusion, famous chips, step-by-step metallurgy, clockmaking and instruments, laboratory chemistry, medicine, telecommunications, software, ships, aircraft and spacecraft. Texts now load as needed; this can be switched off under Layers.
